original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Independent adversarial audit of PR6114 (head 3183c655): its theorem (constant invertible entry, literal p16 Laurent alphabet: twisted outputs <= paid odd shears - 1, income <= thick calls - 1) re-derived and replayed with a separate exact engine on the three retained controllers; two gaps in the written proof closed (left boundary, lift cancellation via the determinant); scope corrected with an explicit per-job Sylvester bound, one positive generalization (one-destination jobs y <- u y + sum f_j x_j with u nonzero and even and any Laurent f_j obey the bound) and three exact escape controls (paid odd translation, Laurent entry boundary, two-row job).
scope_change_reason: Drawn from the adversarial-audit track (the overnight coordinator flagged it as under-served; its uniform-transfer and supplier-boundary cards are PR6030-adjacent and PR6030 already had six follow-ups tonight). The audited result belongs to the joint-query-controller card, so this package keeps that card and audits its newest unreviewed result instead of building a new controller.
bottleneck_link: PR6114 argues that the controller rank-mass income per port is capped at thick calls minus one, leaving the owned centre and local-word fragmentation as the complex-side levers. The audit confirms the cap for the literal alphabet and states exactly which changed primitives or interfaces can exceed it, so a later controller search knows which hypothesis it must change.
stop_rule: Stop at a confirmed or refuted theorem with an exact, independently replayed check of the three literal controllers and exact controls for each scope claim; do not audit the surplus formula M or the moment.

open_questions.question: Is there a legal physical primitive realizing Escape 1 (a paid odd central translation Q^{+-1} on one bank) or Escape 2 (a supplier boundary that already carries odd Q content) at the P104 caller, and what does it cost?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Either would raise the controller income from thick - 1 to thick per port (104 rank units on the PR5907 word) without the multi-bank primitive that PR6114 names as the only escape.
open_questions.first_step: Price Q^{+-1} as a native job in research/p104-productive-controller/caller.py physical() terms (it is a translation by the port axis q with a phase), and check whether its rank charge is below one unit per port.
open_questions.blocked_by: Native/physical realization of an odd translation; the literal alphabet rejects it as a free event.

open_questions.question: Which multi-row paid jobs (rank A_o >= 2 or singular A_e) are physically available, and is the even-rank drop they buy worth their charge?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The Sylvester bound in PROOF.md A4 makes the per-job twist capacity (n - rank A_e) + rank A_o computable before any search.
open_questions.first_step: Compute (n - rank A_e, rank A_o) for each candidate paid job in an existing supplier inventory and compare with its paid rank.
open_questions.blocked_by: An inventory of multi-bank paid primitives with prices.
